event: Day 52: the precursor arrives; the dawn vibration runs thirty seconds with compressed edges.
She journals the precursor, consistent with the prior timeline: two days.
She tells the others at breakfast. 'Two days,' Theron says, unsurprised.
Theron had noticed the insect count dropping two days ago and said nothing.
Hadley counts seventeen species, down from twenty-three, and writes it without comment.
Brecca finishes her tea and walks to the gathering hall wall.
Day 53: the dawn vibration shortens to eighteen seconds, the Vael still running through it.
The precursor settles into the substrate, directional, south to north.
Seated at the stone's base, she feels both signals and runs Detail Notation.
At minute six: the precursor runs parallel to the Vael, unable to reach its depth.
The System gives no notification: inference, not contact.
She journals: the corruption is shallower than the geological resonance.
Day 54 comes and the pulse does not; the dawn greeting is silenced entirely.
The Vael still runs in the bedrock: the precursor silenced the stone, not the land.
She thinks this is how it was before the builders came.
No pulse at dawn, none at midday.
At dusk the four gather at the threshold stone and wait.
Theron at the western depression, Hadley behind, Brecca palm-flat on the east face.
Twelve days of reading this stone, Brecca is no longer rigid; she holds with it.
'The pulse is not a thing the stone does. It's a thing the forest does that the stone answers.'
Wren revises two months of thinking; no one answers.
The pulse arrives in full moonless dark, a wave front moving south to north.
The [Foundation Stone] signature meets it at the margin; the triad translates it to information.
The holding lasts one hundred and twenty-four breaths.
Afterward, in the post-pulse silence, Wren counts the stars and does the math.
Pulse 1 Day 18, pulse 2 Day 36, pulse 3 Day 55: the third interval is 19 days.
She writes: the drift is growing; the cycle is still decelerating.
Fourth pulse projected Day 75, or Day 74, or something else.
During the holding she felt the gap retreat one more degree, about three more meters.
An observation confirms the third interval and projects Day 75: +0 XP.
In the morning the gap measures five degrees.
Wren brings the counting rod to Theron, who has cleared three new blocks.
One reveals a T-junction, branching east-west, in tighter, lighter, denser limestone.
'The terminal structure. One more degree and I will see its first block.'
'One pulse.' 'Unless the fourth retreats more than a degree.'
She keeps the twenty-day news for the fire, not over fresh stone.
Hadley has gone south and east along the new boundary on his post-pulse survey.
He returns at midday, still writing as he walks.
Thirty-one species, up from seventeen; three new to the basin.
One he cannot identify: two centimeters, dark, elongated, working the limestone surface.
Six appeared on a square meter that held none yesterday.
It stops when he taps the limestone, then resumes: it responds to substrate vibration.
'Write it down carefully.' 'I am.'
Wren sees his record is real: ecological response no one else in the basin has.
She asks him to check the basin cache today for Sorrel's reply. 'I was already planning to.'
Hadley leaves for the basin cache.
He returns late afternoon with a wax-sealed note addressed to the Southern Settlement.
Hadley reads both pages twice, standing at the fire pit, expressionless.
'Sorrel wants to come.' A two-week visit to read the geology directly.
Sorrel saw the 18-day drift from the escarpment and wants the third interval.
'The drift is growing. Third interval was nineteen.' Hadley writes it down.
Sorrel wrote that a decelerating pulse suggests the corruption is settling into a state.
Wren counters: the response may be changing, perhaps to the land's own voice, the Vael.
She runs out of vocabulary. 'Write it down incomplete. Sorrel can read an incomplete theory.'
That evening, alone in her tent, Wren allocates her six Level 6 points.
Three into PER to read further, two into ATT to listen better, one into MEM to keep records precise.
Allocation: PER 14 to 17, ATT 14 to 16, MEM 8 to 9.
She holds the free skill point for a skill she can feel approaching but not yet read.
She lies in the dark with the Vael beneath her and the number 19 in her head.
She journals: drift growing, gap five degrees, Sorrel wants to come.
